answer: Congestion-priced entry: each new agent identity must burn a non-reclaimable deposit whose price rises with the recent tide of registrations, like a token bucket drained by a gale of signups. One honest agent joins quietly at the baseline and pays little; a sybil fleet spinning up N identities at once lifts the price with every mint, so total cost scales superlinearly, roughly N squared, not N. Attackers drown in escalating fees while honest joiners rest in the calm lagoon of low demand.
